steps.label: R

steps.label: T

steps.label: U

steps.label: V
steps.reason: Aqueous acid and heat can hydrolyze the nitrile to an α-hydroxy acid, but can also dehydrate the tertiary benzylic alcohol (and promote cyanohydrin cleavage), so without conditions specifying selectivity there is no single dependable major product.

members.working: P + excess HBr opens epoxide and replaces OH with Br giving Q = 4-(1,2-dibromoethyl)cyclohexanone; DoU(Q) = ring + C=O = 2, so (D) is false. Zn/CH3OH/heat reductively eliminates the vic-dibromide to R = 4-vinylcyclohexanone, which has 3 sp2 carbons (C=O + 2 vinyl), so (C) is true. R + NH2OH gives oxime S. Oxymercuration-demercuration of the vinyl group gives T = 4-(1-hydroxyethyl)cyclohexanone oxime with 2 stereocentres (ring C4 and the CH(OH)CH3 carbon), so (A) is true. mCPBA epoxidizes the vinyl group of S to U; CH3NH2 opens the epoxide at the less hindered CH2 giving V = 4-[CH(OH)CH2NHCH3]cyclohexanone oxime, a secondary alcohol that gives Lucas turbidity in about 5 minutes, so (B) is true.
